approach: Official Pearson content order for the three options studied here: Paper 1 option 10, Paper 2 British depth study B1 and Paper 3 option 31. No textbook organisation has been supplied.

included_options: 10 (Crime and punishment in Britain, c1000–present, with Whitechapel, c1870–c1900)
excluded_options: Paper 2 British depth studies B2, B3, B4
Paper 2 period studies P1 to P5 (the other booklet of every Paper 2 combination)
scope.not_edexcel_options: Vikings and a local-history site study (Verulamium) are not options in this specification; no content was invented for them.

points.content: The local context of Whitechapel. The problems of housing and overcrowding. Attempts to improve housing: the Peabody Estate. Provision for the poor in the Whitechapel workhouses. Links between the environment and crime. Life in Whitechapel as an inner city area of poverty and discontent.

points.content: The inhabitants of Whitechapel. The lack of employment opportunities and level of poverty. The impact of changing patterns of migration: the settlement of migrants from Ireland and Eastern Europe, and the increase in Jewish migration during the 1880s.

points.title: The organisation of policing in Whitechapel
points.content: The organisation of policing in Whitechapel. The role of the ‘beat constable’. The work of H division and the difficulties of policing the slum area of Whitechapel, the rookeries, alleys and courts. Problems of policing caused by crime and antisocial behaviour: alcohol, prostitution, protection rackets, gangs, violent demonstrations and attacks on Jewish people.

points.content: Investigative policing in Whitechapel: developments in techniques of detective investigation, including the use of sketches, photographs and interviews; problems caused by the need for cooperation between the Metropolitan Police, the City of London Police and Scotland Yard. Dealing with the crimes of Jack the Ripper and the added problems caused by the media reporting of the ‘Ripper’ murders. The Whitechapel Vigilance Committee.
